prompt: Two teams count arrivals on different sides of the same service step. What should change in the next increment?

options.text: Order detectors to get a larger set of arrival records.
options.feedback: Additional records will still have two interpretations until the event order is agreed.

options.text: Agree on event order, record the decision and rerun the comparison.
options.feedback: The disagreement affects the meaning of the result. A small, reviewable rerun makes the investigation useful again.

options.text: Replace the long-term aim for the intersection.
options.feedback: The ambiguity concerns an experiment. It provides grounds to revise the increment while the stakeholder aim still guides planning.

prompt: A team wants to keep its direction while learning whether the fixed-phase model is useful. Which entry belongs in its immediate backlog?

options.text: Improve how people move through the intersection.
options.feedback: That describes a longer-term outcome. A backlog item identifies a concrete piece of work toward it.

options.text: Set the full hardware procurement schedule.
options.feedback: Procurement depends on choices that this investigation is meant to inform.

options.text: Write down how each slot treats arrivals and check one trace together.
options.feedback: The task can be done and reviewed within the next increment. Its result gives the team grounds to keep or revise the plan.
